what_its_for: Calcitonin salmon is used to treat osteoporosis (weak, brittle bones) in women who have gone through menopause. It helps slow down bone loss and may reduce the risk of spine fractures. It can also be used to treat high calcium levels in the blood (hypercalcemia) and a bone disease called Paget's disease.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a nasal spray. Before using it for the first time, you must prime the pump by holding the bottle upright and pressing down on the pump until a fine mist appears (usually 5 to 10 pumps). Blow your nose gently before each use. Tilt your head slightly forward, insert the tip of the bottle into one nostril, and press the pump once to release one spray. Alternate nostrils each day — use the right nostril one day and the left nostril the next day. Do not blow your nose right after using the spray. Throw away the bottle after 30 doses even if there is medicine left inside.
dosing: The usual dose for osteoporosis is one spray (200 units) into one nostril once a day. Your doctor may prescribe a different dose depending on your condition. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Take calcitonin salmon at the same time each day to help you remember.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not use two doses at the same time or in the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store unopened bottles in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Do not freeze. Once you open a bottle and start using it, you can keep it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 30 days. Store the open bottle upright. Keep away from heat, direct light, and humidity. Keep all medicines out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid blowing your nose right after using the spray, as this can reduce how much medicine gets absorbed. Tell your doctor if you notice any nasal problems such as crusting, bleeding, or pain. Avoid using other nasal sprays at the same time without asking your doctor first. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you feel dizzy after using this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you have: a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, or dizziness; nosebleeds or significant nasal irritation; new or unusual bone, joint, or muscle pain; nausea or vomiting that does not go away; swollen hands or feet; or any signs of low calcium such as muscle cramps, numbness or tingling in your fingers, toes, or lips. Also tell your doctor if you have any changes in your mood or unusual symptoms.
when_it_works: Calcitonin salmon begins working to slow bone loss fairly quickly, but you will not feel this happening. It may take several months of regular use before your doctor can measure improvements in bone density through a bone scan. It is important to keep taking this medicine even if you do not feel any different. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular check-ups and bone density tests.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is not typically recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or nursing. Kidney or liver problems: Use with caution; your doctor may need to monitor you more closely. Allergies to fish: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to fish or salmon, as this medicine is made from salmon and could cause a serious allergic reaction. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine and should be monitored carefully by their doctor.
